URL: https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/06/treasury-yields-inch-lower-as-investors-look-ahead-to-key-jobs-data-.html
Outlet: CNBC, published Fri Nov 6 2026 4:34 AM EST, updated Fri Nov 6 2026 4:01 PM EST. By Sarah Min, Sawdah Bhaimiya, Sean Conlon
10-year Treasury yield rises after much stronger-than-expected October jobs report

10-year Treasury yield: 4.864% (increased more than 2 basis points)
30-year Treasury bond yield: 5.263% (climbed more than 1 basis point)
2-year Treasury note yield: 4.522% (advanced more than 4 basis points)

October non-farm payrolls: 165,000 jobs added; unemployment rate 4.1% (down from 4.2%); economist expectations 59,000 jobs and unemployment holding at 4.2%; September: only 29,000 jobs were added.

Christopher S. Rupkey, chief economist at FWDBONDS: "Fed officials are likely wishing they hiked rates last week" and "the latest red hot labor market data" will complicate inflation efforts. "One thing is certain and that is interest rates are going higher, much higher."

December 9 Fed meeting: 77% probability of a quarter-point hike (up from 66% previously). Current Fed funds rate: 3.75% to 4.00%.

Context: Nasdaq, S&P 500 and Russell 2000 experienced their worst single day since April 2025; "Magnificent Seven" stocks lost more than $1 trillion in aggregate market cap.
